items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta Interview, 1957-03-21
items.q: Martha Bobcats is a feature of Bob. Bob Crosby.

ctx.x: . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . Yes, sir. What was the name of that? . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . When did you first hear that number? Is that a new number or more? It's about 1935 or something. Why sure. Have you ever played it down here before? I mean some parts of it. Why sure. You know the feature of that? That was Glenn Miller's. You learned that off the record or something? You heard them playing? Oh yeah.

Glenn Miller. Now you take Martha Bobcats. Martha Bobcats is a feature of Bob. Bob Crosby. And Boogie Woogie. Pine Top Smith. Featured by Tommy Dawson. I have to play Boogie was out. He played it good too.

Did you ever hear George Thomas play any of that kind of blues? Somebody told me, I believe Clarence Williams once told me that George Thomas was the first one he heard play that Boogie bass. You remember George Thomas of course. Oh yeah, I remember George Thomas piano player. Yes, played in the district. I think he had made that New Orleans. New Orleans. New Orleans. New Orleans. New Orleans.
